title: Hoagy Carmichael, 'Rockin' Chair' and Armstrong's genius
summary: Armstrong accepted any tune brought into the studio, leaving Russell to make arrangements, and Holmes calls him a genius.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: That happened with "Mahogany Hall Stomp" and "Old Rockin' Chair". Hoagy Carmichael walked in. "Louis, I want you to do this (?). Can you record this for me?" [POPS' VOICE] "Yeah, man. Yeah, man." He'd never say no. He'd
never say "No, I won't record it." Poor Russell had to get up the ideas for the arrangement.

But Louis, I mean, he was... He was a genius. There was nothin' he played that sounded bad! I've been listening to some of his records, you know. I said, "Damn, I guess he was pretty good." His records sure sound different.
